column.text: Bitcoin ETFs swung back to net outflows, and the Thursday 22 Oct print was $635.5M out. The seven-day net is still +$103.9M, so the selling is fresh while the buying is aging. Ether is the weaker link. Its ETFs shed $110.5M on Thursday 22 Oct and sit at −$484.4M over seven days, which points to real rotation out of the asset rather than a trim. Solana is smaller, at −$8.5M on Thursday 22 Oct and −$41.1M over seven days, but it leans the same way. Derivatives are positioned the other way. The long/short ratio is 2.19, and the desk read flags top Hyperliquid whales as net short. That mix is a squeeze setup if the crowd is wrong, or a flush if support fails. The line to watch is $81k. Bitcoin is already being pulled toward $81,500, and stablecoin supply is contracting, so a clean break there would hit crowded longs hard. Macro offers no help. The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.9%, Brent is trading at $112.37 after a 3.00% intraday surge, and the 10-year yield sits at 5.00%. Dollar liquidity is flat, and Fear and Greed reads 50, neutral. Our regime is risk-off, but a down tape is not a short signal on its own. Shorts need a mechanism you can point to in the printed blocks, and anything below conviction 7 trades at half size. Continuation longs need real momentum, meaning rising open interest and price plus a reclaim of the 20-day MA, not a headline bounce. Hold $81k and the squeeze trade gets interesting. Lose it and the flush arrives on its own schedule.
